newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel evicts bedouin to expand Jewish settlement.
newsitem.headline: Israel evicts bedouin to expand Jewish settlement.

text.p: Israeli police evicted Palestinian bedouin and flattened their West Bank encampment on Monday to make room for expansion of a Jewish settlement, witnesses said.

They said about five Palestinians were hurt as police pushed bedouin of the Jahalin tribe who refused to vacate their shacks down an embankment. Israeli bulldozers demolished about 20 wood and tin shacks and police removed one tent from the site.

"We have carried out an evacuation of four families to an alternative site. There was a little resistance but it wasn't violent," Peter Lerner, a spokesman for the Israeli civil administration in the West Bank, told Reuters.

Israel has been trying to evacuate about 350 Jahalin bedouin, who live off grazing sheep and menial labour near the Arab village of Aizariyeh east of Jerusalem to make room to expand the Jewish settlement of Maaleh Adumim.

The Israeli military authorities say the bedouin are squatting on state land designated since 1981 for the expansion of Maaleh Adumim. The evictions came after the Jahalin tribe lost a legal battle in Israel's Supreme Court last September.
Lerner said Israel had offered the bedouin to move to an alternative site fitted with electricity and water. He said each family would be given a plot of land to build a new home.
But the bedouin, who say they have lived at the site since the 1950s, argue that the new Israeli-built site is located close to a grabage dump and would cause health hazards.
Police evicted one bedouin family earlier this month and warned others to leave on their own or face forceful evictions.
Witnesses said Monday's evacuation began when police ringed the encampment and gathered the young men on a hill to prevent possible violence while workmen began clearing the site.
They said scuffles broke out after police dragged away bedouin who refused to leave. Police pushed four or five Palestinians over a five-foot high embankment and some of the men fainted as they fell.
Medics treated them on the spot while workmen continued to haul the Palestinians' belongings into a truck.
Lerner said at least two people were detained by police while their families were put on a bus to carry them to the new site.
